title: Inheritance, mixins, polymorphism, and cooperative super
sources: Python 3.14 Tutorial, Classes: inheritance and multiple inheritance; Python 3.14 built-in functions: super(); Python 3.14 Data Model: class method resolution; reviewed 2026-10-03
masterChecklist: Inheritance, composition, mixins, multiple inheritance, MRO, super, polymorphism
whyItMatters: A subclass or mixin can add behavior, but multiple inheritance becomes surprising unless you understand which method runs next. A small example lets you predict that order before building a larger design.
simpleExplanation: Inheritance says a specialized class can use and extend behavior from a base class. Polymorphism means callers can use different objects through the same expected operation without checking each concrete class. A mixin is a narrow class intended to contribute one behavior, often without standing alone as a domain object. In multiple inheritance, Python computes a method resolution order (MRO); Class.__mro__ shows the order. super() delegates to the next class in that order for the current instance, not necessarily to one named parent. A cooperative chain works only if each participating override calls super() and its signatures are compatible. Composition—a class holding a collaborator—is often easier than a wide inheritance hierarchy.
mentalModel: Think of a line of helpers. Each helper may wrap the work, then hand it to the next helper in a defined queue. super() means 'next in this queue', not 'my favorite parent'.
outcomes: Read a class's MRO and predict a cooperative call chain.
Explain a narrow mixin and why direct parent calls can skip behavior.
Use one shared method name polymorphically.
Choose composition when a collaborator is more natural than an is-a subtype.

realWorldExample.scenario: A study-report object needs base report text plus a small prefix and audit marker.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Calling Report.render(self) directly from one mixin could skip the other mixin. A class hierarchy built only for small formatting changes can become hard to maintain.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Use an explicit and tested cooperative chain only when the inheritance relationship is justified; otherwise inject small formatting or audit collaborators.

explanation: The MRO lists StudyReport, PrefixMixin, AuditMixin, Report and object in the order Python searches for render.
PrefixMixin calls super(), which continues at AuditMixin; AuditMixin continues at Report. The returned strings are combined while the calls unwind.
StudyReport is a Report subclass, so code expecting Report.render can call it without knowing its concrete type. This is the simple polymorphic contract shown here.
This is a small demonstration, not a recommendation to use many mixins for ordinary reports; composition may be clearer.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Swap PrefixMixin and AuditMixin in StudyReport's base list and predict the new MRO and render output before running.

procedure: Start with the operation callers need, such as render(), and its expected result.
Ask if a collaborator would express the design more clearly; use inheritance only if a true subtype contract exists.
If narrow mixins are justified, make each override call super() with a compatible signature.
Print __mro__ in a small local experiment to confirm method order.
Test the result and a polymorphic call through the base-class interface.

commonMistakes.mistake: Thinking super() always calls a class's visually listed parent.
commonMistakes.why: It follows the runtime MRO for the current instance.
commonMistakes.avoid: Inspect the concrete class's __mro__ and use cooperative calls throughout the chain.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling Report.render(self) directly inside a mixin.
commonMistakes.why: This can bypass another mixin and break the cooperative chain.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use super().render() when every participant is designed to cooperate.

commonMistakes.mistake: Building multiple inheritance solely to avoid passing a small collaborator.
commonMistakes.why: The MRO and state initialization can become more complex than the original task.
commonMistakes.avoid: Consider composition or a plain function for replaceable behavior.

lab.title: Predict and test a cooperative report chain
lab.safety: Fictional in-memory report strings only; no network or personal records.
guidedSteps: Make PrefixMixin.render call super().render() and prepend study: .
Make AuditMixin.render call super().render() and append [checked].
Confirm it is a Report subtype using isinstance.
checks: MRO is StudyReport, PrefixMixin, AuditMixin, Report, object.
Both mixins call super() rather than naming Report directly.
lab.solutionExplanation: Each override hands work to the next class in the MRO, so both mixins contribute exactly once to the final report.
challenges: Predict the output after swapping mixin order.
Find the lost behavior if PrefixMixin calls Report.render(self) directly.
Experiment: replace one formatting mixin with an injected formatter object and compare the design complexity.
lab.testCode:
assert StudyReport().render()=='study: progress [checked]'
assert StudyReport.__mro__[:3]==(StudyReport,PrefixMixin,AuditMixin)
assert isinstance(StudyReport(),Report)
print('PASS: cooperative MRO')

projectConnection.milestone: Choose a clear report extension strategy and document why a mixin or a composed collaborator fits.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: Tests prove the intended render contract, exact contribution order, and one reasonable alternative design using composition.

assessment.question: What does super() follow in a cooperative multiple-inheritance call?
assessment.answer: The current object's method resolution order.
assessment.explanation: It is not simply a hard-coded call to one named parent.

assessment.question: Why can Report.render(self) be a bug inside PrefixMixin?
assessment.explanation: A direct base-class call bypasses the cooperative MRO chain.

assessment.question: When might composition be preferable?
assessment.answer: When a report merely uses replaceable formatting behavior rather than being a genuine subtype hierarchy.
assessment.explanation: Holding a collaborator avoids making method order part of a simple formatting feature.
